# Brand

## Idea

### Brand = intentional pairing, done consistently
<a id="brand-intentional-pairing"></a>

Branding is a pairing of things; good branding is an intentional pairing of relevant things done consistently; brand is the audience's resulting association (Nike + Jordan, Harley + freedom).

> an intentional pairing of relevant things done consistently

`idea` · formats: reel30, reel60, reel90, yt-short, yt-long, carousel, story, podcast · niches: all · stated · from [L05](../sources/L05.md)

Related: [Brand = a title plus one emotion](../topics/brand.md#brand-title-one-emotion)

### Decide what not to be associated with
<a id="brand-anti-associations"></a>

The more important question: what do you NOT want to be associated with (collabs, podcasts, sponsors)? He'd decline even the biggest audience.

> awareness is not worth the trade

### Brand Journey: work backwards
<a id="brand-journey-backwards"></a>

Desired outcome → what you must be known for → what you must do → what you must learn (the last gives day-one actions).

<a id="brand-own-the-gap"></a>

### Brand story: catalyst, core truth, proof
<a id="brand-story-catalyst-truth-proof"></a>

Catalyst (why it exists), core truth (what you believe that others don't, not controversy for its own sake), proof (what you do and prove over and over).

> your brand is not what you say, it's what you do and prove over and over again

### Start narrow, expand in layers
<a id="brand-start-narrow-layers"></a>

Early trust comes from being great at one specific thing; expand only into adjacent topics, once excellent, after consistent engagement or when the audience asks, keeping your roots.

> expand in layers, not leaps

`idea` · formats: reel30, reel60, reel90, yt-short, yt-long, carousel, story, podcast · niches: all · stated · from [L05](../sources/L05.md) · ⚠ [C19](../clashes.md#c19)

### 80/20 interest stacking
<a id="brand-interest-stacking"></a>

80% your core subject, 20% other interests; each extra interest is another "at bat" to connect. Pillars are guidelines, not rules.

> I like to call this interest stacking.

### Positioning: known for, shelf test
<a id="brand-positioning-known-for"></a>

Positioning is what you're known for: not generic, remembered, AI-legible. Shelf test: stand next to everyone in the category and name your reason to exist (Monster = counterculture, Celsius = health).

> positioning is simply what you're known for.

`idea` · formats: reel30, reel60, reel90, yt-short, yt-long, carousel, story, podcast · niches: all · stated · from [L07](../sources/L07.md)

Related: [Counter-position = different, not opposite](../topics/brand.md#brand-counter-position-different)

### Positioning type and one statement
<a id="brand-positioning-types"></a>

Pick one type (performance, category creation, counter, smart, value, niche, generational, single attribute, premium, counter-luxury, name) as north star; write "For [target] who [need], [brand] is the [category] that [benefit]. Unlike [competitor], we [differentiator]."

> This is your north star.

Related: [Closer to the dollars, more money](../topics/business.md#biz-closer-to-dollars)

### Brand world: characters, sets, plot
<a id="brand-world-characters-sets"></a>

Map who can be on camera and every set, then plot it like TV: events, enemies (competitor moves), friends (partners to piggyback), specials (your own series for empty stretches); find the holes and refresh monthly.

> basically plot, we have events, we have enemies, we have friends, and we have specials.

Related: [Series get the best view-to-follower ratio](../topics/growth.md#growth-series-view-to-follower)

### Events calendar: personal, culture, industry
<a id="brand-events-calendar"></a>

A calendar by month or quarter of company/personal events, culture moments (New Year, summer, Black Friday) and industry events (CES, competitor launches).

### Brand = a title plus one emotion
<a id="brand-title-one-emotion"></a>

Tombstone test: what one title would people give you, and can they attach one emotion (Nike = hard work, New Balance = style)?

> can someone give you a title and can they add just one emotion to it?

### Counter-position = different, not opposite
<a id="brand-counter-position-different"></a>

Counter-positioning means different positioning, not opposite; spike into a pocket, then grow out (Amazon with books, Vans with skaters).

> It doesn't mean opposite positioning. It just means different positioning.

### Small right audience beats big wrong one
<a id="brand-follower-quality"></a>

How and on what you grow is what your audience will always be; 10,000 quality followers can change your life. Caleb's 68K landscape-photo followers don't engage with his current topic.

> the way you grow and what you grow on is what your audience will always be.

### One idea beats many
<a id="brand-one-idea"></a>

The strength of an idea is inversely proportional to its scope; "and" on a landing page is rarely good ("We make jeans, that's it").

### Three Instagram strategies
<a id="brand-instagram-strategies"></a>

Expert on camera (Oren's #1, at least 3 posts/week), storytelling about an interesting business (~2/week), or extremely art-directed. People beat brand handles: personalities drive more impact.

> This is the number one most effective and easiest way to promote your business on Instagram.

## Script

### Tell the story, don't claim the trait
<a id="brand-tell-story-not-trait"></a>

Your story is the differentiator: the ~32-hour editing stretch instead of "I'm a hard worker"; Bezos' door desk instead of "resourceful".

> your story is your brand's secret weapon

<a id="brand-tone-fit"></a>

Harry removed Hinge's mascot because Hinge isn't silly (Duolingo is). And if customers feel smart choosing you ("brains instead of wealth"), you did something right.
